nodes.label: TSMC
nodes.relation: Makes NVIDIA's GPU dies and packages them with CoWoS
nodes.summary: TSMC is the only maker of NVIDIA's data center chips and holds most of the world's CoWoS packaging capacity.
brief: Foundry and CoWoS packager
Its CoWoS capacity sets how many GPUs NVIDIA can ship each quarter.
nodes.health: Raised its 2026 sales growth forecast to 44% and kept capex at US$60-64 billion.

nodes.label: SK hynix
nodes.relation: Largest HBM supplier for NVIDIA's Rubin GPUs
nodes.summary: SK hynix supplies most of the HBM stacked next to each NVIDIA GPU and says it is sold out through 2029.
brief: Leading HBM memory supplier
Its HBM volume and price feed straight into NVIDIA's unit count and gross margin.
nodes.health: Record Q3 operating profit of 83.3 trillion won on 104.6 trillion won revenue.

nodes.label: Samsung Electronics
nodes.relation: Second HBM4 supplier, now qualified on HBM4E
nodes.summary: Samsung is NVIDIA's second HBM source, and its 2027 price talks set the floor for memory costs.
brief: Memory maker, second HBM source
Its 2027 HBM pricing decides how much memory inflation NVIDIA must absorb.
nodes.health: KB Securities expects its HBM selling prices to rise more than 100% in 2027.

nodes.label: Micron
nodes.summary: Micron is the smallest of NVIDIA's three HBM suppliers but says its 2027 output is mostly spoken for.
brief: US memory maker, HBM supplier
Its sold-out 2027 HBM confirms memory stays scarce and pricier for NVIDIA.
nodes.health: More than 75% of its 2027 output is already committed to customers.

nodes.label: Foxconn
nodes.relation: Largest assembler of NVIDIA's rack-scale systems
nodes.summary: Foxconn builds a large share of NVIDIA's NVL72 racks, so its server sales are an early read on NVIDIA's shipments.
brief: AI rack and server assembler
Its AI rack sales show NVIDIA systems leaving the factory before NVIDIA reports.
nodes.health: Record Q3 net profit of NT$77.52 billion, up 34%, at a 6.02% gross margin.

nodes.label: Wistron
nodes.relation: Builds GPU boards and servers for NVIDIA systems
nodes.summary: Wistron assembles NVIDIA GPU boards and servers and reports revenue monthly, which makes it a fast data point.
brief: GPU board and server assembler
Its monthly sales give a near real-time read on NVIDIA's data center volumes.
nodes.health: October revenue NT$402.6 billion, up 117.6% from a year earlier.

nodes.label: Kinsus
nodes.relation: ABF substrate maker under a new NVIDIA capacity deal
nodes.summary: Kinsus makes the ABF substrates that every GPU package sits on, a material that has been short all year.
brief: ABF chip substrate maker
Substrates are a hidden cap on GPU output, and NVIDIA is paying to lift it.
nodes.health: Expanding NVIDIA-dedicated ABF capacity more than 3.5x, with full output by Q3 2028.

nodes.label: Amkor
nodes.relation: Outsourced packager adding CoWoS-class capacity for NVIDIA
nodes.summary: Amkor is building packaging capacity in Arizona and Korea, partly funded by NVIDIA, as a second path beyond TSMC.
brief: Outsourced chip packager
Extra packaging lines outside TSMC raise the ceiling on NVIDIA's shipments.
nodes.health: Holds nearly $3 billion of multiyear NVIDIA agreements funding Arizona and Korea expansion.

nodes.label: Intel
nodes.relation: EMIB packaging offered as a cheaper second source to CoWoS
nodes.summary: Intel's EMIB packaging gives custom-chip buyers like Google a way around TSMC's sold-out CoWoS lines.
brief: Rival packaging second source
Cheaper non-TSMC packaging lets custom chips grow without waiting behind NVIDIA.
nodes.health: Its foundry unit lost $10.3 billion on $17.8 billion of revenue in 2025.

nodes.label: US grid equipment shortage
nodes.relation: Transformer and turbine lead times gate when data centers can switch on
nodes.summary: Transformers, switchgear and gas turbines for new data centers now take years to arrive, which can delay rack deployments.
brief: Power equipment bottleneck
If buildings cannot get power, customers slow GPU orders regardless of budget.
nodes.health: Large power transformers now take more than three years to deliver.

signals.headline: TSMC reportedly eyes 20% CoWoS price hike, skips equipment price renegotiations amid AI demand surge
signals.whyItMatters: A packaging price hike proves CoWoS is still the bottleneck, which supports the supply-limited thesis, but it also lands on NVIDIA's cost of goods.
signals.evidence: the foundry giant is reportedly weighing price hikes of up to 20%, with some packaging lead times already stretching

signals.headline: Report: TSMC to double CoWoS capacity by 2028 as AI chip shortage spills over to rivals
signals.whyItMatters: Doubling CoWoS lets NVIDIA ship far more units, but once packaging stops being scarce the pricing support in the supply-limit thesis weakens.
signals.evidence: CoWoS capacity to sit at 260,000 wafers per month by the end of 2028, up from 130,000 at the end of this year

signals.headline: SK hynix 'HBM sold out for three years'... dismisses memory 'peak-out'
signals.whyItMatters: HBM sold out through 2029 keeps GPU supply capped, which props up NVIDIA's pricing, but it also hands the memory makers the pricing power.
signals.evidence: effectively all sold out for the next three years, through 2029

signals.headline: SK hynix reportedly plans new HBM4 equipment orders, with P&T6 in focus despite NVIDIA uncertainty
signals.whyItMatters: SK hynix is adding HBM capacity with Google's TPU in view, so new memory supply is not reserved for NVIDIA and helps custom chips scale.
signals.evidence: P&T6 at full capacity could lift HBM output by more than 20,000 wafers per month; TPU shipments projected to nearly double from 8-9 million units in 2027 to 16-18 million in 2029

signals.headline: Micron blew past estimates and says it can't see when the memory shortage ends
signals.whyItMatters: Micron is charging much more for 2027 HBM, and every dollar of memory inflation NVIDIA cannot pass on comes out of its gross margin.
signals.evidence: A large part of the volume is already sold out for 2027... and the prices are much higher than 2026

signals.headline: Samsung's HBM prices tipped to more than double in 2027
signals.whyItMatters: If blended HBM prices rise 121% next year, the memory bill per Rubin rack climbs sharply and pushes NVIDIA's margin toward the 70% kill line.
signals.evidence: TrendForce forecasts that the global HBM market's blended average selling price will rise 121 percent year-on-year in 2027

signals.headline: Samsung Electronics passes Nvidia quality tests for next-generation HBM4E memory chips
signals.whyItMatters: A qualified second source for HBM4E gives NVIDIA more volume for Rubin Ultra and some leverage against SK hynix on price.
signals.evidence: Samsung's 12-layer HBM4E product reportedly passed qualification tests by Nvidia and major hyperscale customers at the end of September

signals.headline: NVIDIA announces financial results for third quarter fiscal 2027
signals.whyItMatters: The Rubin ramp and pricier memory take the gross margin guide from 74.8% to 71-72%, close to the 70% level that breaks the supply-limit pillar.
signals.evidence: GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be between 71.0% and 72.0%

signals.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) earnings show its best quarter ever, reported while its stock was sliding
signals.whyItMatters: NVIDIA locked in $111 billion more supply, mostly memory, which secures units for years but fixes the cost at today's inflated prices.
signals.evidence: Supply commitments of $390 billion at the end of October, up from $279 billion three months earlier

signals.headline: Hon Hai's Q3 net profit hits record high amid AI boom
signals.whyItMatters: Foxconn's AI racks grew faster than it expected last quarter, so NVIDIA systems are clearing the assembly line at the pace its data center guide needs.
signals.evidence: Net profit NT$77.52 billion, up 34% year on year; AI servers and AI racks grew more than expected in the third quarter

signals.headline: Wistron (3231) reports October revenue of NT$402.6 billion, up 117.6% year on year
signals.whyItMatters: Wistron's sales more than doubling in October points to NVIDIA's January quarter tracking at or above its $130 billion guide.
signals.evidence: October revenue NT$402.615 billion, up 5.7% from September and 117.6% from a year earlier

signals.headline: NVIDIA expands commitments with supply chain partners to support AI infrastructure buildout
signals.whyItMatters: NVIDIA is paying to remove the substrate bottleneck, which protects its 2027 and 2028 unit growth even if T-glass and ABF stay tight industry-wide.
signals.evidence: Kinsus plans to expand its ABF substrate capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by more than 3.5x; added capacity targeted for Q3 2028

signals.headline: NVIDIA expands commitments with supply chain partners to support AI infrastructure buildout
signals.whyItMatters: Funding Amkor gives NVIDIA packaging capacity outside TSMC, so its unit ceiling rises even if CoWoS stays fully booked.
signals.evidence: NVIDIA's multiyear agreements with Amkor total nearly $3 billion and fund advanced packaging expansion in Arizona and South Korea

signals.headline: Google reportedly books Intel for packaging more than 3 million TPUs in 2028
signals.whyItMatters: A cheaper packaging route outside TSMC removes the CoWoS queue that has held back Google's TPU, the custom chip most likely to take NVIDIA share.
signals.evidence: Bernstein estimates EMIB costs a few hundred dollars per chip, versus $900 to $1,000 for CoWoS on a Rubin-class processor

signals.headline: America's grid upgrade hinges on a 400-ton machine designed in the 1800s, and just one U.S. mill makes the special steel inside it
signals.whyItMatters: When transformers take over three years and gas turbines up to seven, customers can have the capex budget but no powered building to put NVIDIA racks in.
signals.evidence: Ordering a large power transformer can take more than three years; gas turbine delivery times have stretched to between three and seven years
